title: Intent, Purpose and Behaviour: what it uses
lede: One arrow for each component this feature lists. The steps reuse the feature's own "how it works" text; nothing here is a new claim. Internal and confidential: this text comes from an internal Ping deck and has not been tested on our tenant.

steps.title: Intent classification
steps.what: Intent classifies what a request is actually trying to do, such as exfiltrating data, changing a payee or looking up a single record, rather than what it literally says, combining deterministic patterns with semantic similarity.
steps.why: A tool name and its arguments say what was asked for, not what it was for, whether this agent was ever meant to do it, or whether it normally behaves this way.

steps.title: Purpose declaration on the agent key
steps.what: Policy can refuse calls that fall outside that declaration, violate a specific axis of it, or arrive from a key that declares no purpose at all, which turns "this agent was issued for invoice reconciliation" from documentation into something enforceable.
steps.why: A tool name and its arguments say what was asked for, not what it was for, whether this agent was ever meant to do it, or whether it normally behaves this way.

steps.title: Behaviour baseline
steps.what: Behaviour: Privilege learns each agent's normal pattern of calls and scores how far a request departs from it, by anomaly level, a target it has never touched, or an argument shape it has never used.
steps.why: A tool name and its arguments say what was asked for, not what it was for, whether this agent was ever meant to do it, or whether it normally behaves this way.

steps.title: Alert and human approval

steps.title: Hard refusal tier
steps.what: Hard refusals rest on the deterministic tier, while the scored signals drive alerts and human-in-the-loop approval, so a model's judgement never silently becomes the enforcement decision.
